spec.title: Namib
spec.subtitle: A coast of fog, dunes, and forgotten ships

chapters.label: CHAPTER 01 · COASTAL MIST
chapters.heading: Fog rolls from the cold ocean onto the dunes.
chapters.subheading: Moisture from the sea breathes life into the desert.
chapters.body: The Namib stretches over two thousand kilometres of Atlantic coast. Along the shore fog forms when the cold Benguela Current meets warm air, creating a belt that can linger for more than one hundred eighty days each year.

heroImage.attribution: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

chapters.label: CHAPTER 02 · SAND SEA
chapters.heading: Waves of sand rise like silent cliffs.
chapters.subheading: A sea of colour that shifts with light.
chapters.body: The southern dune sea between Lüderitz and the Kuiseb River holds some of the world's tallest dunes. In Sossusvlei dunes exceed three hundred metres in height. Their pink and orange hues shift with the sun, a silent ocean of sand.

heroImage.attribution: Giles Laurent · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

chapters.label: CHAPTER 03 · SKELETON SHORE
chapters.heading: Shipwrecks lie half buried in shifting sand.
chapters.subheading: Remnants of voyages lost to fog.
chapters.body: The Skeleton Coast bears a graveyard of more than a thousand wrecks, victims of fog and fierce currents. Ships such as the Eduard Bolen lie hundreds of metres inland, swallowed as the desert slowly advances toward the sea. Lions prey on seals on the Skeleton Coast.

heroImage.attribution: Yathin S Krishnappa · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

unsupported.text: This moisture sustains lichens, succulents and the desert's hidden life.
